                            , Tyson Goulding <tyson.goulding@optconnect.com> wrote:

 Hi Teal Support, We're troubleshooting a payment-transaction failure for a customer's terminal in Canada. The evidence points to the TLS handshake failing on the public-egress path for one of our SIMs on the lattigopriv APN, and we'd like your help characterizing what happens on your side. Domains: aprivawebservices.trafficmanager.net & paymentwebservice.apriva.com via 51.143.124.200 The SIM: ICCID 8901990000005060358 (IMSI 204080930355844), assigned IP 100.81.201.96 on the lattigopriv APN. What we see (device diagnostic loop, 2026-08-20, per-phase timing DNS -> TCP -> TLS): - The device resolves and TCP-connects to the payment host (https://www.google.com/url?q=http://ws.accounts.apriva.com&source=gmail&ust87431307491000&sa=E -> https://www.google.com/url?q=http://51.143.124.200:443&source=gmail&ust87431307491000&sa=E) in ~0.4s, every cycle. - The TLS handshake then goes silent and times out at 10s, every cycle. TCP up, TLS dead. This is not a device or application problem. The customer put a completely different SIM, from another provider, into the same physical terminal, and the identical payment transaction to the same host completed normally. Same hardware, same app — so the terminal is fine; the failure follows this SIM's connection. The private path is healthy. The device's traffic over our tunnel to the customer datacenter returns HTTP 200 throughout — including during the exact windows the public TLS handshake is timing out. Only the public egress for this SIM is affected. From the device telemetry, we can see our SIM is attaching to a tower that appears to be TELUS-owned, which raises the question of whether a roaming or inter-operator issue is affecting the egress path. Our questions: 1. For SIM 8901990000005060358 / IP 100.81.201.96 on lattigopriv, are there any known roaming or egress issues affecting its public-Internet path — particularly to https://www.google.com/url?q=http://51.143.124.200:443&source=gmail&ust87431307491000&sa=E? 2. What public egress IP is this SIM NAT'd to on the way out, and do you see the outbound TLS session to https://www.google.com/url?q=http://51.143.124.200:443&source=gmail&ust87431307491000&sa=E leaving your gateway with return traffic from the server? 3. Is there any MTU / MSS / fragmentation handling or a stateful firewall / DPI policy on the lattigopriv egress that could drop the larger packets of a TLS handshake while allowing the small TCP handshake packets through? We can share the raw device logs if that would help. OptConncet Network Engineering Team

--

 Tyson Goulding

text.content: Current sprint is 38 tickets and only 1 done, so most of this is going to roll. Here’s what I’d put at the front of next sprint.

First: Chris’s 60-day Teal exit. That isn’t a ticket yet. Next sprint should open an epic, name a PM, and start inventorying Teal lines. [NETE-737](https://optconnect.atlassian.net/browse/NETE-737) is the live fire (Teal 22995, still In Progress on Andy). Pull that over until Teal answers or you have a cutover path.

Also sitting Urgent in this sprint: [NETE-722](https://optconnect.atlassian.net/browse/NETE-722) NovaCharge overage (Andy, Pending Review). Close it or roll it, don’t let it sit.

Your own Urgent item is [NETE-713](https://optconnect.atlassian.net/browse/NETE-713) (host 10.50.1.124 remediations), plus two unassigned twins in the backlog, [NETE-662](https://optconnect.atlassian.net/browse/NETE-662) and [NETE-667](https://optconnect.atlassian.net/browse/NETE-667). All three have been To Do since June.

After that, the work that actually has a clock on it: T-Mobile’s extra private-APN tunnels (Nancy’s note from today, no ticket I can see), Monday’s Level Parking IPSec and Jeff M2M ATT, and [NETE-518](https://optconnect.atlassian.net/browse/NETE-518). The WS4 ATT/Verizon API tickets on you ([NETE-619](https://optconnect.atlassian.net/browse/NETE-619), [NETE-622](https://optconnect.atlassian.net/browse/NETE-622) and the NetSuite twins) are already Pending Review, so those are close-out, not new build.

High in the backlog I’d only pull if there’s room: [NETE-720](https://optconnect.atlassian.net/browse/NETE-720) PagerDuty migration and [NETE-721](https://optconnect.atlassian.net/browse/NETE-721) Stryten SG CDK. Netbox and Unimus ([NETE-729](https://optconnect.atlassian.net/browse/NETE-729), [NETE-730](https://optconnect.atlassian.net/browse/NETE-730), [NETE-94](https://optconnect.atlassian.net/browse/NETE-94)) stay as your in-flight, not new commitments.

Want me to open a Teal-exit epic so the 60-day clock has a home?

text.content:
Nothing new since Wednesday. [NETE-722](https://optconnect.atlassian.net/browse/NETE-722) is still Urgent, Andy, Pending Review.

On Aug 17 Jonathan sent the Canada eSIM logs Andy asked for (ICCID 8901990000000830912, IP 100.81.161.51). Andy’s read: Teal is split-tunnel too. OCPP to `ocpp.chargeupev.com` goes through our IPsec (`10.100.90.1`). Public (google.com) exits Teal’s gateway and never hits us. Same story as the AT&T physical SIM. That explains a path for overages, not the bill itself. We still don’t have usage-by-destination.

Ball is with NovaCharge. Mark emailed Oscar Aug 19 asking for general deployed regions (not street addresses) so Sales can propose a true-private plan. Oscar hasn’t answered. Andy noted the same on the ticket that afternoon. No mail on that thread since.

input.prompt:
Describe what is happening in the attached video, in detail.

This is a ~5.5s screen recording of a demonstration on a Linux desktop. Frames already show Google Chat at chat.google.com/app/home, signed in, Home selected, Unread filter on, Net-Eng spaces in the sidebar.

Give a structured play-by-play:
1. Starting state (what page or app was open)
2. Every meaningful action in chronological order (clicks, typing, navigation, URL changes, menus, scrolling, buttons)
3. Ending state
4. Approximate timing
5. Exact text typed (search queries, form values) — NEVER transcribe passwords, one-time codes, or other credentials; note only that a credential was entered

Be specific about URLs, page titles, entity names, and UI elements clicked. If they open a space, name it. If they click a conversation, name the sender and subject.

# Find Chrome DevTools endpoint for display :2, then GET /json/list. Copy History sqlite read-only.
# Stay read-only: no /json/new, no websocket, no cookies scrape.
set +e
echo "=== chrome procs ==="
ps aux | rg -i 'chrom' | head -40
echo "=== debug ports / cmdline ==="
for p in /proc/[0-9]*; do
  cmd=$(tr '\0' ' ' < "$p/cmdline" 2>/dev/null)
  echo "$cmd" | rg -q 'chrome|chromium' || continue
  echo "$p $cmd"
done | rg -i 'remote-debugging|devtools|user-data' | head -20
echo "=== common ports ==="
for port in 9222 9223 9333 18888 18889; do
  curl -sS -m 2 "http://127.0.0.1:$port/json/list" && echo "PORT=$port" && break
done
ls /tmp 2>/dev/null | rg -i 'chrome|devtools|cdp' | head
# find user-data-dir
ud=$(ps eww -C chrome -o args= 2>/dev/null | head -1)
echo "ps chrome: $ud"
rg -l 'user-data-dir' /proc/*/cmdline 2>/dev/null | head

executableCommands.name: head
executableCommands.fullText: head ud=$(ps eww -C chrome -o args= 2>/dev/null | head -1) echo "ps chrome: $ud" rg -l 'user-data-dir' /proc/*/cmdline

      "id": "1a02699c2e145dc7",
      "snippet": "Hi Tyson, Thank you for reaching Teal Communications Support Team and for bringing this to our attention. We will investigate the issue from our side to determine why the TLS handshake is timing out",
      "subject": "Re: 22995 | Issue accessing domain, this is for one of our customers",
      "sender": "support@tealcom.freshdesk.com",
      "toRecipients": [
        "tyson.goulding@optconnect.com"
      ],
      "ccRecipients": [
        "support@tealcomminications.com",
        "net-eng@optconnect.com",
        "m2msupport@optconnect.com"
      ],
      "date": "2026-08-21T23:13:23Z",
      "plaintextBody": "Hi Tyson, Thank you for reaching Teal Communications Support Team and for bringing this to our attention. We will investigate the issue from our side to determine why the TLS handshake is timing out despite the TCP connection being successful, we’ll work on and check: Roaming and public-egress issues The SIM’s public NAT/egress IP Outbound and return traffic to 51.143.124.200:443 Any MTU/MSS, fragmentation, firewall, or DPI issues Possible network-side issues with the destination Thank you for your patience and for providing the detailed diagnostics. We’ll investigate further and get back to you with our findings. Regards,  Jacky Teal Support Team

                            On

                            Fri, 21 Aug at 4:09 PM

                            , Tyson Goulding <tyson.goulding@optconnect.com> wrote:

 Hi Teal Support, We're troubleshooting a payment-transaction failure for a customer's terminal in Canada. The evidence points to the TLS handshake failing on the public-egress path for one of our SIMs on the lattigopriv APN, and we'd like your help characterizing what happens on your side. Domains: aprivawebservices.trafficmanager.net & paymentwebservice.apriva.com via 51.143.124.200 The SIM: ICCID 8901990000005060358 (IMSI 204080930355844), assigned IP 100.81.201.96 on the lattigopriv APN. What we see (device diagnostic loop, 2026-08-20, per-phase timing DNS -> TCP -> TLS): - The device resolves and TCP-connects to the payment host (https://www.google.com/url?q=http://ws.accounts.apriva.com&source=gmail&ust87431307491000&sa=E -> https://www.google.com/url?q=http://51.143.124.200:443&source=gmail&ust87431307491000&sa=E) in ~0.4s, every cycle. - The TLS handshake then goes silent and times out at 10s, every cycle. TCP up, TLS dead. This is not a device or application problem. The customer put a completely different SIM, from another provider, into the same physical terminal, and the identical payment transaction to the same host completed normally. Same hardware, same app — so the terminal is fine; the failure follows this SIM's connection. The private path is healthy. The device's traffic over our tunnel to the customer datacenter returns HTTP 200 throughout — including during the exact windows the public TLS handshake is timing out. Only the public egress for this SIM is affected. [routine] "NovaCharge follow-up" (folder novacharge-follow-up) is due — Every 2 hours on weekdays, 8:43 AM – 6:43 PM (43 8-18/2 * * 1-5), fired 8/24/2026, 10:47:51 AM.
This is your own routine firing on schedule, not a message the user just typed.
What you saved to do each time:
Finite watch: NovaCharge overage / NETE-722. Tyson wants to know when they reply on the Gmail thread "OptConnect - NovaCharge - Follow up meeting" (thread id 19f4328b797f7491).

Last known mail: Mark Parreno on 2026-08-19 ~2:19 PM MDT asked Oscar Rodriguez for general deployed regions (not street addresses). Andy already analyzed the AT&T physical SIM (split tunnel) and the Canada Teal eSIM logs Jonathan sent 2026-08-17 (ICCID 8901990000000830912, IP 100.81.161.51). Ticket NETE-722 is Urgent, Andy, Pending Review. No reply since Mark's Aug 19 chase.

On each run: look up Gmail tools first (schema may have changed). Search for new mail on that thread or from jonathangilbert@novacharge.net / oscarrodriguez@novacharge.net / marilynrodriguez@novacharge.net about NovaCharge / NETE-722. Ignore everything through Mark's 2026-08-19 follow-up.

If they reply (regions, more logs, billing, a meeting, anything new), tell Tyson immediately: who wrote, what they said, and whether NETE-722 needs an update. Then delete this routine.

If nothing new, stay quiet.

Deadline: if this is still running on 2026-09-04 with no reply, tell Tyson the watch expired and delete this routine.
If the instruction mentions a skill (e.g. @Some skill), read that skill file from your workflows folder with Shell and run it as part of this — the mention is a pointer, not a copy.
If the saved instruction spells out a specific MCP tool call, treat its arguments as possibly stale — this routine may have been written long ago — and confirm the current schema with your MCP tool-discovery tool before relying on them.
Carry it out now. If there's something worth surfacing, tell the user how it went with SendMessage — casually, the way you'd mention something you remembered to handle, not by announcing a routine. If the saved instruction above says to stay quiet when there's nothing to report and there's nothing new, just end the run with no SendMessage rather than sending filler like "(no change.)"; nobody is waiting on this. If it can't be done, SendMessage to say why. If you're already mid-task with them, don't stop: finish that first, then slip this in as a "btw …" aside. Keep it self-contained — the schedule asked for this, not the user just now.

You are receiving this message because your VPN Connection vpn-0e3b691c8a991d18e in the us-west-1 Region had a momentary lapse of redundancy as one of two tunnel endpoints (Tunnel Outside IP: 13.56.36.146) was replaced. Connectivity on the second tunnel was not affected during this time. Both tunnels are now operating normally.

Replacements can occur for several reasons, and be initiated either by AWS or when you modify your VPN Connection [1]. AWS-initiated replacement reasons include health, software upgrades, and when underlying hardware is retired.

AWS Site-to-Site VPN includes two tunnels so that you can maintain a highly available VPN connection. If you have configured your VPN Customer Gateway to use both tunnels, then your VPN Connection will have utilized the alternate tunnel during the replacement process. For more on tunnel endpoint replacements, please see our documentation (2). If you have not configured your VPN Customer Gateway to use both tunnels, then your VPN Connection may have been interrupted during the replacement. We encourage you to configure your router to use both tunnels. You can obtain the VPN Connection configuration recommendations for several types of VPN devices from the AWS Management Console [3]. On the "Amazon VPC" tab, select "VPN Connections". Then highlight the VPN Connection and choose "Download Configuration".

You are receiving this message because your VPN Connection vpn-07bb7e8b20d3305cf in the us-west-1 Region had a momentary lapse of redundancy as one of two tunnel endpoints (Tunnel Outside IP: 54.177.215.211) was replaced. Connectivity on the second tunnel was not affected during this time. Both tunnels are now operating normally.

Replacements can occur for several reasons, and be initiated either by AWS or when you modify your VPN Connection [1]. AWS-initiated replacement reasons include health, software upgrades, and when underlying hardware is retired.

This replacement was AWS Initiated.

AWS Site-to-Site VPN includes two tunnels so that you can maintain a highly available VPN connection. If you have configured your VPN Customer Gateway to use both tunnels, then your VPN Connection will have utilized the alternate tunnel during the replacement process. For more on tunnel endpoint replacements, please see our documentation (2). If you have not configured your VPN Customer Gateway to use both tunnels, then your VPN Connection may have been interrupted during the replacement. We encourage you to configure your router to use both tunnels. You can obtain the VPN Connection configuration recommendations for several types of VPN devices from the AWS Management Console [3]. On the "Amazon VPC" tab, select "VPN Connections". Then highlight the VPN Connection and choose "Download Configuration".
